<description>
Use CoinsViewOverlay to speed up ConnectBlock in TestBlockValidity. This also has the benefit of not inserting entries fetched from db into the main cache.

cs_main must be held for each place where the overlay is being used, and the reset guard ensures it will be reset for the next caller.
</description>

[quoted text omitted]

Before #35295, coins were fetched as validation reached each transaction, so any failure avoided fetching later transactions, but `StartFetching()` can now retain those coins before validation rejects the template.

In normal block connection this is gated behind PoW, so paying for that work to allocate an extra ~250 MiB on a node (~25k max inputs × 10 kB max script sizes) seems like a poor trade-off for an attacker. Not sure if this can be amplified in any way by the threads or if it's a total (probably the latter).

But I wonder if this changes the threat model here, given that these template checks aren't behind PoW.
[2026-10-07] r:5438004859 review CHANGES_REQUESTED by l0rinc (member):

[2026-10-07] rc:4208127181 inline on src/validation.cpp by andrewtoth (member) (edited 2026-10-07):
[quoted text omitted]

I'm not sure I follow why an attacker would bother creating an invalid block here? If the goal is to have the node allocate ~250MB, they could create a block that spends ~25k distinct utxos with 10kb scripts. Why would they bother creating an invalid block to do this, instead of creating a valid one and keeping the block reward? I also don't see how #35295 changes anything here; this would allocate the same amount of memory before or after that PR.

[quoted text omitted]
I don't think TestBlockValidity can be called via any untrusted paths, so any threat-model is substantially reduced.
